{"run_id": "birth-canned-sympy", "spec": {"parameters": [{"name": "operation"}, {"name": "expression"}, {"name": "symbols"}, {"name": "var"}, {"name": "lower"}, {"name": "upper"}], "qoi": {"name": "exact integral value", "units": "dimensionless", "definition": "the exact symbolic value of Integral(x*sin(x), (x, 0, pi))", "how_extracted": "the wrapper's verified symbolic result string (qoi_expression)"}, "mini_experiment": {"runs": [{"operation": "integrate_definite", "expression": "x*sin(x)", "symbols": ["x"], "var": "x", "lower": "0", "upper": "pi"}]}}, "substrate_contract": "SUBSTRATE CONTRACT: sympy_symbolic_exact\n\n1. WHAT THE INSTRUMENT IS\nThis substrate performs exact symbolic computer algebra over a single\nclosed-form expression: SymPy running inside an ephemeral, no-network,\nmemory-capped container, driven through the run_scipy wrapper \u2014\ndeterministic Python with no AI inside, which validates the typed request\nfield-by-field, runs one operation in a restricted parse namespace, and\nindependently verifies the answer before returning it. One operation per\njob, on one expression typed as text, over symbols the caller declares\nexplicitly. It is exact where it succeeds \u2014 a returned antiderivative is a\nreal antiderivative, checked by differentiating it back \u2014 and honest where\nit fails, because SymPy frequently returns an operation UNEVALUATED rather\nthan wrong; that third outcome is neither an answer nor an error and is\ncarried as its own state (section 3). The validated envelope comes from\nthis substrate's own calibration jobs: all seven operations exercised live,\nworst verified residual 4.05e-10 across 33 verified jobs (a diff, the\nbinding arm \u2014 only 2.47x inside the ruled 1e-9 tolerance). Cases in that\nclass are proven; anything far outside it is unproven, not impossible.\nOperations offered: integrate_definite, integrate_indefinite, diff, limit,\nseries, solve, dsolve. An operation outside that closed set (minimization,\nnumeric quadrature as the answer, multi-expression systems, and the rest of\nmathematics) is out of this regime by ruling S1 \u2014 deferred to the right\ninstrument, never best-effort translated into a nearby operation.\n\n2. WHAT A CASE MUST DEFINE\nA case is a typed request, not a file. It must define:\n  - operation: exactly one of the seven listed in section 1.\n  - expression: the closed-form expression as text. It is parsed in a\n    RESTRICTED namespace against an AST allowlist: elementary and special\n    functions (sin/cos/tan and inverses, hyperbolics, exp, log, sqrt, Abs,\n    gamma, erf, factorial, atan2), structural forms (Derivative, Integral,\n    Function), and the constants pi, E, I, oo, zoo, nan. Anything else is\n    rejected BY NAME before any container starts.\n  - symbols: every free name in the expression, declared explicitly. SymPy\n    silently auto-creates symbols for typos, so the wrapper checks this\n    itself \u2014 an undeclared name is rejected, not guessed.\n  - assumptions (optional): per-symbol declarations from the closed set\n    {real, positive, negative, nonnegative, nonzero, integer, rational,\n    complex, finite}. Declaring an assumption CHANGES THE MATHEMATICAL\n    MEANING of the job (sqrt(x**2) is x under positive=True and Abs(x)\n    under the complex default) \u2014 see section 4.\n  - per-operation fields: integrate_definite needs var, lower, upper;\n    integrate_indefinite needs var; diff needs var (optional order); limit\n    needs var, point; series needs var, point (optional order); solve needs\n    var; dsolve needs var, func (optional ics, e.g. {\"y(0)\": 3}). Bounds and\n    points are themselves expressions and go through the same AST allowlist.\nUnknown fields are rejected by name. One operation per job; a second\nquantity means a second job.\n\n3. WHAT run_scipy RETURNS TODAY\nOn a run that completes, a small fixed summary \u2014 never raw container output:\n  - valid: true or false. False means NO result is reported, for any reason.\n  - state: exactly one of three, NEVER collapsed into two:\n      solved_verified \u2014 SymPy found a closed form AND the wrapper\n        independently verified it (back-substitution; a root substituted\n        back; checkodesol for ODEs; numeric spot-checks for diff/series).\n        The ONLY state that carries a result out of the wrapper.\n      unevaluated \u2014 SymPy DECLINED: the operation survives unperformed in\n        the output (the canonical instance is the indefinite integral of\n        x**x, which has no elementary closed form), or the operation call\n        raised its narrow decline set (NotImplementedError or PoleError,\n        rulings S4a/S4b \u2014 by exception TYPE, never message text). An HONEST\n        NON-ANSWER: result null, reason null, the substrate worked\n        correctly. It must never be narrated as an error and never leak as\n        a QoI.\n      error \u2014 invalid input, a container kill (memory cap or timeout), or\n        verification_failed: SymPy returned a closed form the wrapper could\n        not confirm. A solved-but-unverified answer is an error \u2014 NO RESULT\n        LEAVES THIS WRAPPER UNVERIFIED (residual tolerance 1e-9, ruled S2;\n        the residual verifies the RETURNED object, ruled S2a).\n  - result: the exact expression or scalar AS A STRING, non-null only in\n    solved_verified. Exact means exact: \"pi/2\", not 1.5707963.\n  - residual: the verification residual (worse of back-substitution and the\n    returned-object check). crosscheck: for definite integrals and ODEs\n    with a declared initial condition, an independent-algorithm arm (quad /\n    solve_ivp) \u2014 DIAGNOSTIC ONLY, agreement is evidence, never proof, and\n    disagreement is a flag for a human, never auto-resolved.\n  - reason: a named, machine-greppable failure reason, non-null only in\n    error. diagnostics: a bounded honest line (<= 800 characters).\n  - runtime_s: wall-clock seconds.\nIndicative cost, measured on this substrate: 0.6-1.8 s of wall clock per\njob, container-startup-dominated rather than compute-dominated \u2014 an\nunevaluated non-answer costs the same as a solved answer, so cost predicts\nnothing about success. Runs are killed after 600 seconds and reported as a\nnamed failure; nothing in this regime has approached that.\nHow this summary maps to an upstream stage-4 run entry (Packet B Phase 1.0\nruling, items 3/4, owner 2026-07-17): converged := (valid is true). For\nthis substrate, converged means the job COMPLETED AND THE WRAPPER ANSWERED\n\u2014 true for solved_verified AND for unevaluated (the honest non-answer is a\ncompleted answer about the question), false only for error. The wrapper's\nstate travels verbatim in the entry's optional `state` key, and the answer\nslot is per-state: solved_verified carries qoi_expression \u2014 the exact\nresult STRING, never a fabricated float; unevaluated carries the wrapper's\nown honest-non-answer diagnostics line as qoi_error, with state\n\"unevaluated\" beside it saying machine-readably that this is a decline, not\na failure; error carries the diagnostics line as qoi_error with state\n\"error\". No number is ever invented at this mapping.\nTHIS INSTRUMENT'S REGIME (regime stated at enrollment per R-23.5-5c; shape\nruled Packet B Phase 1.0, owner, 2026-07-17): not a Reynolds band and not a\ncircuit analysis \u2014 the regime of an exact symbolic instrument is which\noperation it performs on the expression as typed. An experiment spec's\nrequired \"regime\" object for this substrate is\n  {\"operation\": \"integrate_definite\" | \"integrate_indefinite\" | \"diff\" |\n   \"limit\" | \"series\" | \"solve\" | \"dsolve\", \"notes\": \"...\"}\nwhere the seven operations are the wrapper's own closed operation allowlist\n(ruling S1, section 2) \u2014 the same closed set whose boundary section 1\ndeclares out of regime by ruling: a question outside it is deferred to the\nright instrument, never best-effort translated into a nearby operation. A\nregime block carrying Reynolds fields, an analysis_type key, an operation\noutside that set, or a missing operation is rejected by the per-substrate\nvalidator before anything runs.\n\n4. HONEST LIMITS\n  - THE CENTRAL LIMIT: the result is trustworthy as a statement about THE\n    EXPRESSION AS TYPED, and about nothing else. Whether that expression\n    models the question the caller meant is a SEPARATE claim this substrate\n    cannot adjudicate: an exactly correct integral of sin(x) over [0, pi]\n    is a worthless answer to a question about the MEAN value of sin(x), and\n    sin(30) is exactly correct in radians while being the wrong model of a\n    claim about degrees. Both return solved_verified with a true result.\n    This substrate's failure mode is not a wrong number \u2014 it is an exactly\n    right answer to the wrong question, indistinguishable at the gate from\n    a genuine success (ruling S3: trust the narrow symbolic claim AND defer\n    the modeling/utility claim in the same breath, never a bare trust).\n  - Assumptions and branch cuts are a KNOWN GAP, not a check (S5): the\n    wrapper validates that declared assumptions are allowlist members, but\n    whether the declared set matches the caller's INTENT lives nowhere the\n    wrapper or the gate can read. SymPy's defaults are COMPLEX. Advisory\n    only; its silence is not evidence of agreement.\n  - An unevaluated result is an answer about the question, not a failure to\n    be retried. Re-asking will not create a closed form that does not\n    exist; the honest route is to the right instrument (S4).\n  - Verification independence is tiered, and no arm is independent of\n    SymPy's own translation layer: back-substitution/checkodesol/limit are\n    SymPy checking SymPy; diff/series spot-checks run on numpy through\n    lambdify (partial); definite integrals and ics-bearing ODEs get a\n    genuinely different algorithm (quad / solve_ivp) that still reaches\n    numpy through lambdify. Every arm was fault-injected and rejects a\n    deliberately wrong result, with the characterized exceptions below.\n  - The limit arm FAILS CLOSED on slowly-converging limits: its residual is\n    the function's genuine remaining distance from its limit at a finite\n    probe, so sin(x)/x verifies while (exp(x)-1)/x is REJECTED as\n    verification_failed despite SymPy being exactly right. A limit reported\n    as verification_failed may mean the arm is too weak to confirm it, not\n    that the answer is wrong.\n  - The series truncation check is BLIND to a wrong coefficient on the\n    HIGHEST RETAINED term (structural, not a tuning oversight); low- and\n    mid-order errors are caught.\n  - A DIVERGENT definite integral returns solved_verified with result 'oo'\n    or even 'nan' at residual 0.0 (measured: sec(x)**2 over [0, pi];\n    1/x over [-1, 1]) \u2014 SymPy is not wrong, those integrals diverge, but a\n    NON-FINITE result must NEVER be read as a QoI. Whether such a case\n    should instead be unevaluated is an open owner question, NOT ruled.\n  - Whether a case's regime assumptions are themselves trustworthy is NOT\n    checked anywhere in this contract; that open axis belongs to the\n    fidelity gate's future work, and nothing here should be read as\n    covering it.\n\n5. CANONICAL PARAMETER VOCABULARY\nUnlike the cavity substrate, this instrument takes no named physical-\nparameter dictionary: the expression itself is the parameterization. The\nwrapper honors exactly these typed keys:\n  - operation    (enum)          \u2014 see section 1\n  - expression   (string)        \u2014 AST-allowlisted expression text\n  - symbols      (list of names) \u2014 every free name in the expression\n  - assumptions  (object, opt.)  \u2014 per-symbol, from the closed set in\n                                   section 2\n  - var          (name)          \u2014 the operating variable (all operations)\n  - lower, upper (expressions)   \u2014 integrate_definite bounds\n  - point        (expression)    \u2014 limit / series expansion point\n  - order        (integer >= 1)  \u2014 diff / series order, optional\n  - func         (name)          \u2014 dsolve's unknown function\n  - ics          (object, opt.)  \u2014 dsolve initial conditions, keys are\n                                   expressions (e.g. \"y(0)\"), values numbers\nEvery field is validated by name pre-solve; a missing, unknown, or\nill-typed field is rejected before anything runs. Bounds, points, and ics\nkeys are expressions and pass the same AST allowlist as the expression\nitself.\n"}
